instruction: Explain overfitting in machine learning to a high school student in simple terms.
response_a: Overfitting is when a model learns the data too well, and it starts to make mistakes on new data that wasn't used during training. It happens because the model has learned patterns from the training data but doesn't generalize well to new situations. This means that the model may not be able to predict future outcomes accurately. Overfitting can happen in many different ways, such as by using too much data or by having too few examples for each feature. To prevent overfitting, we need to use techniques like regularization (such as L1 or L2 regularization) and cross-validation to ensure our models are not too complex and don't memorize the training data.
response_b: Overfitting is when a model learns the data too well, and it starts to make mistakes on new data that wasn't used during training. It's like trying to fit a toy car into a real car race track - you can't do much with just one toy car because it won't be able to compete with the real cars. Overfitting happens when the model becomes so good at predicting the training data that it doesn't learn from any other data that isn't included in the training set. This means that the model will have trouble making accurate predictions on new data that didn't even exist during training time. Overfitting can happen in many different ways, such as by using too few examples or not enough features for the model to learn.

The glucose produced during photosynthesis can be used by the plant or used by other organisms that consume it.
